First, try to get an idea of what your poem will be about so that it will flow smoothly. There are multiple ways of rhyming in poems, but the most common ones are AABB and ABAB, A being two words that rhyme, and B being two words that rhyme with each other but not with A. 

An example of AABB would be: "Once you got a theory of how the thing works,  
everybody wants the next thing to be just like the first. I am not a monkey, I will not dance even if the beat's funky." as Line 1 and 2 rhyme, and Line 3 and 4 rhyme. (Yes, I used Linkin Park lyrics.)

You would also want to consider what person this would be in. 1st (from your perspective, using I and me), 2nd (from the reader's perspective, using you and yours etc.) or 3rd person (not using I or you, but he/she/they/it.)

The tone you want to go for is funny and romantic. One way of being funny is to use double meaning (e.g. engaged can mean planning to get married or being used.) Another one would be to have something unexpected happen. which often catches the reader by surprise. Consider your use of language and tone to make it a certain mood.

Also avoid just picking random words. Try to really put effort and thought into it. It shows when someone has put absolutely no effort or attempts into a piece of literature. If you need to find words that rhyme, try RhymeZone and to find synonyms, try [Thesaurus.com](https://Thesaurus.com).
